title: Career Roadmap · QC Analyst
summary: A Quality Control (QC) Analyst tests raw materials, in-process samples and finished products to check whether they meet quality, safety and specification requirements. Duties vary across food, dairy, leather and other manufacturing industries.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Food Technology / Dairy Technology / Leather Technology or another relevant laboratory discipline

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Science; Chemistry is particularly useful. Biology or Mathematics may be required by specific programmes.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Chemistry, biology, mathematics, microbiology and basic statistics.

blocks.label: Entrance/admission
blocks.text: State polytechnic entrance or merit-based admission, depending on the course.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Laboratory testing, sampling, product defects, hygiene and quality standards.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Accurate measurement, documentation, attention to detail and laboratory safety.

items.text: Diploma in Food Technology → Food QC Technician / Laboratory Assistant.
Diploma in Dairy Technology → Milk and dairy-products testing roles.
Diploma in Leather Technology → Leather testing and materials QC.
B.Sc. Chemistry / Microbiology / Biotechnology → Relevant laboratory analyst roles, depending on employer requirements.
B.Tech Food Technology / Chemical Engineering → Industrial quality-control and process-quality roles.
B.Sc. / B.Tech in a relevant discipline → Broader testing, quality assurance and specialist laboratory pathways.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.text: Some QC Analyst positions require a bachelor’s degree, specific subject qualifications or relevant laboratory experience. A diploma does not automatically meet every employer’s eligibility criteria.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Chemistry, microbiology, laboratory safety, measurement and sampling.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Analytical testing, product specifications, instrument handling and test records.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: Industrial lab experience, calibration, defect analysis and quality documentation.

blocks.label: Year 4 (degree route)
blocks.text: Advanced analytical methods, validation, research project and career preparation.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Food-quality comparison • Dairy sample testing • Leather material-property analysis • QC defect-tracking dashboard.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Recognised academic qualifications, subject prerequisites, transcripts, English or other language proficiency where applicable, and visa documentation. Research degrees may require a relevant prior degree and research proposal.
Check each institution’s current programme and admission requirements.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: QC Analyst, Laboratory Technician, Food Testing Analyst, Materials Testing Technician.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Food, dairy, leather, chemicals, pharmaceuticals and independent testing.
Employers may require a degree, local laboratory standards knowledge or professional recognition. Overseas employment and visa sponsorship are not guaranteed.
